newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 27.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 27. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The West Java town of Tasikmalaya was paralysed on Thursday after rioting in which a police station, shops, churches and factories were attacked and destroyed.
Indonesia's non-oil trade deficit is expected to turn around next year with the government prediciting this year's $450 million deficit will become a $900 million surplus next year.
The Indonesian Association of Wood Panel Producers (Apkindo) has not revised its export targets for 1997 because it expects the price of plywood will increase by 20 percent next year.
Religious leaders have condemned the riots in Tasikmalaya as emotional and irresponsible actions which could threaten national stability.
West Java's military commander Major-General Tayo Tamadi said the rioting in Tasikmalaya was not a spontaneous action by the crowd.
